correctness.rationale: For complex lambda outside −2,−1,2, the given Ciani quartic is smooth and the source produces exactly 28 distinct explicit bitangent lines in three symmetry families of sizes 4,12,12. The derived square restrictions and identities under lambda=−2(t^4+1)/(t²+1)² establish bitangency, and the classical 28-bitangent theorem proves completeness. The inspected exact SymPy certificate computes each of C(28,3)=3276 determinants (36 generically zero), factors the 3240 nonzero polynomials, maps all 45 t-factors by exact resultants to 16 parameter strata (13 smooth, 3 singular), checks squarefreeness/disjointness, and recovers incidence points by line-pair closures, with 378 line pairs each time. Independent direct determinant incidence reconstructions confirmed generic (324,0,9), and sample exceptional spectra (312,4,9), (288,12,9), (252,24,9). The complete source certificate, not merely the four independent samples, supplies the remaining 16-factor exhaustion. Triple points occur at exactly 1+10+13=24 distinct smooth lambda; lambda=0 and lambda²+3lambda+18 produce only quadruple jumps; no multiplicity ≥5.

originality.rationale: Janasz–Pokora–Zieliński analyze this exact Ciani pencil, and provide three specialized bitangent-arrangement tables plus a uniform lower bound on quadruple points. Their inspected primary §3 does not provide the complete discriminant of triple concurrence, which is a different incidence invariant; coincidence of the family does not itself mean coverage. Classical automorphism/bielliptic-involution accounts for some quadruple structure, not 24 explicit triple-concurrence parameter values. Resultary searches yield nearby quartic arrangement studies without the same all-parameter polynomial. Older specialized incidence tables remain a credible originality risk.
